title: Convert India and China hub traffic

blocks.text: 3.1.2 Source market growth and diversification

The second theme is about which markets grow the base. It holds three focus areas: India and China, the fastest-growing markets, which reach the province through hubs; the mature long-haul markets; and regional Africa. Volume and value come from different groups, so each needs its own lever (section 2.2).
Theme 1.2 · Source market growth and diversification · Focus area 4
Convert India and China hub traffic

About 101,000 Indian and Chinese travellers a year already reach Cape Town, mainly through Gulf and African hubs, and with no direct Indian route likely before 2030, converting that flow is the lever available now.
The opportunity

India and China grow fastest in the base case, at 8% a year to 2035, against 5% for the Middle East and Brazil in their acceleration group (Market Assessment Report, May 2026, p22). India and China start from a low base, at about 2.6% and 1.4% of South Africa's overseas tourists in September 2025 (Current State Diagnostic, Dec 2025, p30). The upside is large, and much of it is already in the air.

About 71,000 Indian and about 30,000 Chinese travellers reach Cape Town each year through Gulf and African hubs (Demand-Side Analysis, Jun 2026, p46, p48). They fly with carriers whose Cape Town business is built on onward traffic. Nine in ten of Qatar Airways' Cape Town passengers connect through its hub, as do more than 80% of Emirates' (MIDAS Aviation Market Assessment, Mar 2026, "Seasonality"). Hub routes through Dubai, Addis Ababa and Doha run at 65.2% to 72.3% load, so they have room for more (MIDAS Aviation Market Assessment, Mar 2026, "Seasonality").

The province is absent where these travellers decide. Both markets plan and book on their own platforms, where Western Cape product is hard to find (section 2.2). Access and product add friction. Cape Town has no direct flight to Mumbai or Delhi and thin Indian-friendly adaptation, while Chinese travellers face complex visas and few Mandarin-language services (Demand-Side Analysis, Jun 2026, p51).

blocks.message: India and China reach Cape Town only through hubs, and the direct route that would change that is at least five years away.

blocks.text: The upside comes in two parts. The hub flow is available now, on routes with spare seats and carriers that gain from every connecting passenger. The direct route is not: the accelerated case depends on confirmed direct routes, and without them volume reverts to base (Demand-Side Analysis, Jun 2026, p20). This focus area therefore works the hub flow now and builds the route case for later.

A further pool is already in the country. Most of South Africa's visitors from India and from China with Hong Kong never reach the province, though they hold a visa and a seat (Wesgro Research, Tourism Source Market Analysis, Nov 2025, p3, p4, computed; section 2.2). Itineraries sold through Johannesburg, with a flight to Cape Town on the same ticket, can reach them.
The course of action

Wesgro should run India and China as conversion markets through the hubs and as relationship markets for the direct route. The money shifts toward trade-led conversion rather than broad awareness (Demand-Side Analysis, Jun 2026, p55). India needs early relationships with its carriers and authorities. China is a long-term investment in which awareness and indirect volume come before any non-stop service (MIDAS Aviation Market Assessment, Mar 2026, "The Indian Market Opportunity", "The Chinese Market Opportunity"). By November 2025 Cape Town Air Access had held talks with Cathay Pacific, China Southern, Air India and IndiGo (Cape Town Air Access, Letsema Update, Nov 2025, slide 13).

The hub work comes first because it needs no new seats. Wesgro agrees joint market support with the three hub carriers in 2027, and activation on the Chinese and Indian platforms runs in market from 2028 (section 4.3). The direct route cases wait for runway capacity and go to carriers from 2032. Wesgro's plan targets three international tourism marketing campaigns over FY26 to FY30 (Wesgro, Strategic Plan 2025/26 to 2029/30, p20). Any that run in India or China should convert inside the platforms and with the hub carriers.

rows: Secure added frequency from Emirates, Qatar Airways and Ethiopian Airlines, with joint market support tied to Indian and Chinese sales
Activate inside Xiaohongshu, Douyin and MakeMyTrip with market-specific itineraries and Trip.com packages
Build long-term route cases for the India and China corridors and keep a standing relationship with Indian carriers, Cathay Pacific, China Southern and China Eastern
Sell Johannesburg-gateway itineraries, with a flight to Cape Town added to the ticket, to Indian and Chinese visitors already bound for South Africa
Ready the product for both markets: Mandarin and Indian-language guiding, Alipay and WeChat Pay, visible vegetarian options
Escalate visa processing for China and India, and the route designation for China that is decided government to government

blocks.text: Why it can work

Conversion works here because the travellers are already moving. Each Indian or Chinese visitor routed to Cape Town fills a seat the hub carrier already flies. The carrier gains from joint marketing without adding capacity. Activation inside the platforms where these travellers plan and pay reaches them at the point of decision, which broad awareness does not.

Singapore converts transit into visits through its Stopover Programme and Free Singapore Tour, run by the tourism board, Changi Airport Group and Singapore Airlines under one strategy (Global Benchmarking Report, Mar 2026, p40). It received 16.5 million international visitors in 2024 and record receipts of about S$29 billion, though no source isolates the programme's share (Singapore Tourism Board, Feb 2025). The condition is visas and the hubs themselves. A Gulf hub disruption would cut connecting capacity, so the work spreads across Dubai, Doha, Addis Ababa and Istanbul (section 4.8).
